alcance:
Use case: scientific-educational.
Asset type: Spanish classroom sketch for CyberColombia PowerPoint, wide 2:1, intended for 1100px JPEG.
Primary request: explain FOUR levels of software testing using a simple shopping application. No overall title: the slide will have its own editable title. Four open hand-drawn scenes in a tight 2x2 arrangement, WITHOUT UI cards, decorative boxes or a pyramid. No arrows between scenes because these levels are not a rigid sequence.
Top left label exactly "Unitaria". Show a single small isolated calculation gear with a tiny plus sign. Under it exact text "Una función". Top right label exactly "Integración". Show one application module connected to a database. Under it exact text "Partes que colaboran". Bottom left label exactly "Sistema". Show a browser, application server and database together, with a light hand-drawn outline encompassing the complete system. Under it exact text "Aplicación completa". Bottom right label exactly "Aceptación". Show a person discussing a checklist with a small application screen. Under it exact text "Necesidad del usuario".
Meaning: unit isolated calculation, integration checks connections between components, system checks whole application, acceptance assesses agreed user needs. Acceptance is not a bigger piece of code and must not be drawn as the top tier of a size pyramid. Distinguish the scenes clearly with visual spacing, not interface panels.
Style: friendly lightweight technical sketch, crisp dark-blue ink, restrained cyan and purple accents consistent with CyberColombia, pure white background, large readable Spanish labels with correct accents. Minimal balanced padding above/below, fill the canvas tightly. No extra text, code, logos, gradients, paper texture or photorealism. Never use a title with the formula "De X a Y" or equivalent.
proposito:
Use case: scientific-educational.
Asset type: compact Spanish educational sketch for CyberColombia PowerPoint, landscape 2:1, reduce to 1100px.
Primary request: explain four PURPOSES of software tests as four questions about the same application. No overall title because it will be editable on the slide.
Center: small simple laptop labelled exactly "Software". Four clearly spaced scenes around it connected by thin undirected lines, without arrowheads. Top left a checklist and gear, large label "Funcional", question exactly "¿Hace lo acordado?". Top right a padlock protecting data, label "Seguridad", question exactly "¿Protege datos y acceso?". Bottom left a stopwatch alongside several simultaneous user requests, label "Rendimiento", question exactly "¿Responde bajo carga?". Bottom right a small code edit and repeated checklist with a check mark, label "Regresión", question exactly "¿Conserva lo que funcionaba?".
Meaning: these are purposes that can overlap and apply at different test levels. Do not draw them as a sequence or hierarchy. Do not imply regression is rollback. Show a repeated check after a change rather than a reverse deployment arrow.
Style: lightweight hand-drawn dark blue ink, sparse cyan/purple highlights, pure white background, large clear Spanish text and accents. Tight crop, minimal top/bottom white padding, no UI cards, no decorative border, no tiny code, no extra words, logos, gradients, paper texture or photorealism. Avoid title formulas such as "De X a Y" or any equivalent.
hoy:
Use case: scientific-educational.
Asset type: compact sketch map of today's actual teaching tests in LibreReserva for CyberColombia PowerPoint, landscape 2:1, readable reduced to 1100px. No overall title; the slide supplies it.
Primary request: three large open scenes side-by-side, connected conceptually by a single small checklist below labelled exactly "Pruebas de hoy". Thin undirected lines from the checklist to each scene, no flow arrows or implied architecture links between the scenes.
LEFT: heading exactly "Reglas de reservas". Draw two calendar intervals touching at their boundary and a small function gear. Below exact text "Intervalos y conflictos". Tiny check symbol. This is domain testing, no database required.
MIDDLE: heading exactly "Respuestas de la API". Draw a small test client sending two requests to an API laptop. Show two response labels exactly "201" and "409". Below exact text "Crear y rechazar solapamientos". This is in-process HTTP TestClient testing, NOT actual load balancing or external network.
RIGHT: heading exactly "Consulta parametrizada". Draw an SQL instruction sheet beside a separate value tag, both going to a small database. The database must be labelled exactly "SQLite en memoria". Below exact text "Ejemplo aislado". This is a teaching demonstration separate from the API and NOT a PostgreSQL adapter test. Do not connect this SQLite database to the middle API.
Do NOT depict PostgreSQL, cloud, Caddy, Kubernetes, performance testing or production deployment as required tests today. There will be an editable slide note about optional PostgreSQL. Do not show an attack payload or code here: it is a map of objects being tested, not the detailed exploit demonstration.
Style: friendly clean hand-drawn technical sketch with dark-blue ink and sparse cyan/purple accents, pure white background, large readable correctly accented Spanish labels. Tight balanced framing, minimal empty top/bottom margin, no UI card grid, no border, logos, photorealism, gradients or paper texture. Never use a title framed as "De X a Y".
